## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Otaraṇahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying Ways of Entry: Analysis", Ne 15) is a chapter of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Netti) [SuttaCentral]. As an analytical exposition (*vibhaṅga*) of the *otaraṇa-hāra*—one of the interpretive devices (*hāra*) for conveying or guiding discourse into fundamental doctrinal frameworks—the section analyzes key doctrinal categories such as dependent origination, the aggregates (*khandha*), and sense bases [Stuart; DharmaNexus]. In section 15.49 (PTS 79–80), the text defines the meaning of aggregate (*khandhattha*) through the notions of collective combination (*samūhattha*), accumulation (*puñjattha*), and heap (*rāsattha*) [Stuart]. Daniel Stuart observes that this characteristic definitional formula is shared with the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pet 6.60) and an unpublished Gāndhārī commentary on the *Saṅgītisūtra*, indicating possible exegetical connections to Buddhist traditions of Greater Gandhāra [Stuart].
SuttaCentral notes that the chapter connects with numerous canonical and paracanonical discourses, including the *Channasutta* (SN 35.87), *Kāma Sutta* (Snp 4.1), *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1), *Catutthanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.4), *Visākhā Sutta* (Ud 8.8), *Kāmajātaka* (Ja 467), several parallel chapters in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1, Pe 2, Pe 5, Pe 8), and related Sanskrit verses in the *Udānavarga* and *Śarīrārthagāthā* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects 1,189 matching passages shared across 71 Pali texts, led by the subcommentary *Nettivibhāvinī* (122 matches) and the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12, 128 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Prominent shared segments also appear in the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35, confirming the connection to SN 35.87), *Otaraṇahārasampāta* (Ne 31), *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38), and *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1) [DharmaNexus]. In non-Pali corpora, DharmaNexus records automatic alignments with the Tibetan *Karmaśataka*, *Maitreyaparipṛcchā*, and *Kāśyapaparivarta*, Sanskrit texts including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, and the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
